units.la: Hic mensium laterculus sex versiculis constat, quorum primus menses exhibet cœlestes sive signa Zodiaci quibus reliqui menses respondent. Nam Dius Macedonicus oritur ab ingressu solis in ζυγὸν, i.e. libram, Αμναῖ⊙ ab ejus ingressu in Scorpium, &c. Secundus menses continet Macedonum, Antiochenorum, Pergamenorum, & Ephesiorum. Tertius Syromacedonum & Smyrneorum, qui situ tantùm à Macedonicis differunt. Quartus Paphiorum & Cypriorum. Quintus Bythyniorum. Sextus denique menses diésque Julianos repræsentat, quibus Sol in singula Zodiaci signa ingressus est cùm hæc anni forma instituta fuit, & à quibus mensés hic descripti incipiunt. Nam Macedonum ΔΙΘ, Syromacedonum ὑπερβερεταῖοι, Paphiorum Ἀφροδισίου, & Bythyniorum Ἡρέως unà cum solis in Libram ingressu, incipit Sept. 24. Et sic in reliquis. Quocirca mensium horum ubicunque occurrat mentio, hujus ope laterculi ad Julianos facillimè reducantur. Ex. gr. Epiphanius refert Christum Baptizatum fuisse χρ̄ Παρίως Ἀπρινικ̃, 15 Juxta Paphios Apogonici 16. Epiph. her. 51. E laterculo patet Ἀπρινικ̃ Paphiorum incipere. octob. 24. Ergò dies istius mensis 16 erat Nov. 8. sive ᾧ ἐξ ἐιδ̃ν ποιμῶν, VI. Id. Novembris, ut ipse Pater asserit.
units.tr: This table of months consists of six short lines, of which the first gives the celestial months, that is, the signs of the Zodiac to which the other months correspond. For the Macedonian Dius begins when the sun enters Libra, i.e. the Scales (ζυγὸν), and Αμναῖ⊙ begins when it enters Scorpio, and so on. The second line contains the months of the Macedonians, Antiochenes, Pergamenes and Ephesians; the third, those of the Syromacedonians and Smyrnaeans, who differ from the Macedonians only in situation; the fourth, those of the Paphians and Cypriots; the fifth, those of the Bithynians. Finally, the sixth gives the months and days of the Julian calendar, on which the sun entered each sign of the Zodiac when this form of the year was instituted, and from which the months described here begin. For the Macedonian Dius, the Syromacedonian ὑπερβερεταῖοι, the Paphian Ἀφροδισίου and the Bithynian Ἡρέως all begin on September 24, together with the sun's entry into Libra; and so for the rest. Hence, wherever mention of these months occurs, they can very easily be converted to Julian dates by means of this table. For example, Epiphanius reports that Christ was baptized on χρ̄ Παρίως Ἀπρινικ̃, the 15th [of the month], "according to the Paphians Apogonic, the 16th" (Epiph. Haer. 51). From the table it is clear that the Paphian Ἀπρινικ̃ begins on October 24. Therefore the 16th day of this month was November 8, that is, ᾧ ἐξ ἐιδ̃ν ποιμῶν, the sixth day before the Ides of November, as the Father himself asserts.

units.la: CAP. XIV. De Astronomico Judæorum anno.
units.tr: CAP. XIV. The Jewish astronomical year.

units.la: Judæis duplex observatur annus, unus Lunaris, solaris alter.
units.tr: The Jews observe a twofold year, one lunar and the other solar.

units.la: I. PER annum Judaicum hîc non veterem illum ante Captivitatem Babylonicam iis usitatum indigito, sed recentiorem ac novitium, qui etiamnum iis in usu est: cujus auctor R. Hillel anno Christi 358 perhibetur. Hæc autem est quàm subtilissima anni forma, atque adeò ingeniosa & acuta, ut satis mirari nequeo, quo tandem fato, Judæis, hominibus, uti quispiam arbitraretur, ad tanta non natis, in mentem unquam subiit. Verùm ut alias quascunque anni formas subtilitate sic & difficultate superat, quam tamen nos, quantâ possumus & brevitate & perspicuitate explicare contendemus.
units.tr: I. By the Jewish year I do not mean here that ancient year which they used before the Babylonian Captivity, but the more recent and newer reckoning, which is still in use among them. Its author is said to be R. Hillel, in the year of Christ 358. This form of year is most subtle, and so ingenious and acute that I cannot sufficiently wonder by what fate it ever came into the minds of the Jews, men not born for such matters, as one might suppose. But just as it surpasses all other forms of the year in subtlety, so also in difficulty, I shall try to explain it with as much brevity and clarity as I can.

units.la: II. Annus Judæorum Lunaris duplex est, Astronomicus & Civilis.
units.tr: II. The Jewish lunar year is of two kinds, astronomical and civil.

units.la: III. Annus Astronomicus vel communis est, vel Embolimæus.
units.tr: III. The astronomical year is either common or embolismic.

units.la: IV. Annus communis 12, Embolimæus 13 constat mensibus Lunaribus.
units.tr: IV. A common year consists of 12 lunar months, an embolismic year of 13.

units.la: 1. Nimirum Judæi, pariter ac Athenienses, menses suos ad Lunæ, annum ad solis motum exigunt: quo fit ut Embolismo nonnunquam cohibeatur necesse est, ne extra cardines æquinoctiales effrænatè divagaretur. Annum Embolimæum מעוברת i. e. Prægnantem vocant eò quòd novum quasi mensem in utero gestat.
units.tr: 1. Indeed the Jews, like the Athenians, measure their months by the moon and their year by the motion of the sun. Hence it is necessary that the year sometimes be restrained by an embolism, so that it does not wander unrestrainedly beyond the equinoctial limits. They call an embolismic year מעוברת [me'uberet], that is, pregnant, because it carries a new month, as it were, in its womb.

units.la: V. In anno Astronomico quinque hæc occurrant observauda, Quantitas, menses, Embolismus, epocha & calculus.
units.tr: V. In the astronomical year five things are to be observed here: quantity, months, embolism, epoch and calculation.

units.la: VI. Primò, quoad quantitatem annus communis est dier. 354. hor. 8. 876. Embolimæus dier. 383. hor. 21. 589.
units.tr: VI. First, as to quantity, a common year is 354 days, 8 hours, 876 parts. An embolismic year is 383 days, 21 hours, 589 parts.

units.la: I. Annus enim communis, ut dixi, mensibus 12 constat, quilibet autem mensis Judaicus est dier. 29. hor. 12. helakim 793. quæ duodecies multiplicata producunt anni communis quantitatem d. 354. h. 8. hel. 276. quibus si adjicias alium mensem, Embolimæi quantitatem habebis d. 383. h. 21. hel. 589.
units.tr: I. For a common year, as I have said, consists of 12 months, and each Jewish month is 29 days, 12 hours, 793 helakim. Multiplying these twelve times gives the length of a common year: 354 days, 8 hours, 276 helakim. If you add another month to these, you will have the length of an embolismic year: 383 days, 21 hours, 589 helakim.

units.la: VII. Secundò, mensium Judaicorum nomina, quantitatem ac ordinem hoc pinacidium repræsentat. Menses JUDAICI. | Dies Menf. | Dies Coll. Tishri. | 30 | 30 Marheshvan. | 29 | 59 Casleu. | 30 | 89 Tebeth. | 29 | 118 Shebat. | 30 | 148 Adar. | 29 | 177 Nisan. | 30 | 207 Jiar. | 29 | 236 Sivan. | 30 | 266 Tamuz. | 29 | 295 Ab. | 30 | 325 Elul. | 29 | 354
units.tr: VII. Second, this table sets out the names, lengths and order of the Jewish months. Jewish months | Days of the month | Cumulative days. Tishri | 30 | 30. Marheshvan | 29 | 59. Casleu | 30 | 89. Tebeth | 29 | 118. Shebat | 30 | 148. Adar | 29 | 177. Nisan | 30 | 207. Iyar | 29 | 236. Sivan | 30 | 266. Tammuz | 29 | 295. Ab | 30 | 325. Elul | 29 | 354.

units.la: I. In computo Ecclæsiastico Nisan primus est mensis, in Astronomico autem & civili Tishri, à quo & temporibus Mosaicis annum suum auspicatos fuisse Judæos constat. Hæc autem mensium nomina à Chaldæis accepta sunt: quòd ex eò patet, quòd ante Captivitatem Babylonicam in sacris Scripturis nusquam occurunt. Nam Libri Nehemiæ, Ezræ, Estheris, Danielis, & Zachariæ in quibus leguntur, post dictam Captivitatem conscripti sunt. Sunt autem omnes hi mensis alternis pleni & cavi, hoc est 30, & 29 dierum, ut hic describuntur.
units.tr: I. In the ecclesiastical reckoning Nisan is the first month, but in the astronomical and civil reckoning it is Tishri, from which it is established that the Jews began their year in the Mosaic times. These names of the months, however, were taken from the Chaldeans. This is clear from the fact that they never occur in the sacred Scriptures before the Babylonian Captivity, for the books of Nehemiah, Ezra, Esther, Daniel and Zechariah, in which they are read, were written after that Captivity. All these months alternate between full and hollow, that is, of 30 and 29 days, as they are described here.

units.la: VIII. Tertio, Embolismus est totius mensis Veadar dicti post Adar communem intercalatio.
units.tr: VIII. Third, the embolism is the intercalation of the whole month called Veadar, after the common Adar.

units.la: I. Mensis hic ἐμβόλιμος ideirco interseritur, ut Lunaris eorum annus Solares intra cardines contineretur, & sic Paschalis celebritas intra terminos a Mose constitutos perageretur. Hic mensis ואדר Veadar dictus est, eo quod post Adar communem inseritur, adeo ut in anno Embolimeo duplex sit Adar, prior & posterior; Is autem simpliciter Adar: hic Veadar, i.e. Et Adar, dicitur, 30 diebus constans.
units.tr: I. This month is inserted as an embolism for this reason: so that their lunar year is held within the limits of the solar year, and the Paschal celebration can thus be carried out within the bounds set by Moses. This month is called Veadar [ואדר], because it is inserted after the common Adar, so that in an embolismic year there are two Adars, the former and the latter. The common one is simply called Adar; this one is called Veadar, that is, and Adar, and it consists of 30 days.

units.la: IX. Quarto, Epocha sive radix anni est istud novilunium medium quod aequinoctio Autumnali proximum est.
units.tr: IX. Fourth, the epoch or starting point of the year is that mean new moon which is nearest the autumnal equinox.

units.la: I. Dum Templum staret Hierosolymitanum, & Sanhedrin haberent Judæi, penes istud doctorum Collegium neomenias ἀπὸ τῆς φάσεως indicendi potestas fuit, quo tandem cessante, neomenias suas totumque annum à novilunis mediis computare coacti sunt, utpote quæ faciliora sunt calculatu.
units.tr: I. While the Temple at Jerusalem stood, and the Jews had their Sanhedrin, the power of announcing the new moons from the sighting [ἀπὸ τῆς φάσεως] belonged to that college of teachers. When this ceased, they were compelled to reckon their new moons and the whole year from the mean new moons, since these are easier to calculate.

units.la: X. Quinto, Iudaicus anni sui calculus hisce propositionibus expediatur. XI. I. Calculus hic procedit à sexta hora pomeridiana Hierosolymis.
units.tr: X. Fifth, the Jewish calculation of their year is carried out by the following propositions. XI. I. This calculation proceeds from the sixth hour after noon at Jerusalem.

units.la: I. Etiamsi dies suos ab occasu solis computent Judæi, nihilo minus calculus ab eadem epochâ non proficiscitur, propterea quod solis occidentis momentum in dies singulos variatur, calculus autem Astronomicus à certa quadam epochâ procedere debet. Calculant itaque perpetuò à sexta horâ pomeridianâ Hierosolymis, eâ tamen conditione, ut si ultra dies completos colligantur horæ 18, aut plus, adeò ut meridies diei sequentis attingatur, tunc feria transfertur, ac si ab antecedentis diei meridie calculus procedit, & horæ istæ 18 solidum diem complerent. XII. 2. Mensis quilibet est dier. 29. hor. 12. hel. 793.
units.tr: I. Although the Jews reckon their days from sunset, the calculation nonetheless does not start from that same epoch, because the moment of sunset varies from day to day, whereas an astronomical calculation must proceed from some fixed epoch. They therefore always calculate from the sixth hour after noon at Jerusalem, on this condition: if the hours, 18 or more, collected beyond complete days, so that the noon of the following day is reached, then the weekday is shifted, as if the calculation proceeded from noon of the preceding day, and those 18 hours would complete a whole day. XII. 2. Each month is 29 days, 12 hours, 793 helakim.

units.la: 1. Hæc est Ptolemaica mensis quantitas. Nam helakim 793 in sexagenaria reducta sunt 44′. 3″. 20‴. Mensis itaque Lunaris juxta Judæos pariter ac Ptolemæum est dier, 29. hor. 12. 44′. 3″. 20‴.
units.tr: 1. This is the Ptolemaic length of the month. For when the 793 helakim are converted into sexagesimal fractions, they come to 44′, 3″, 20‴. So the lunar month, according to the Jews as well as Ptolemy, is 29 days, 12 hours, 44′, 3″, 20‴.

units.la: XIII. 3. Epocha calculi Judaici est Molad Tohu.
units.tr: XIII. 3. The epoch of the Jewish calculation is Molad Tohu.

units.la: 1. מולד תהו Molad Tohu est istud novilunium quod, methodi gratiâ, mundi primordium uno anno præcessisse fingitur. Hoc autem novilunium five νουμηνια accidit Octob. 7. anno per. Jul. 953. Ab hâc igitur Epochâ calculus Judaicus semper procedit.
units.tr: 1. Molad Tohu [מולד תהו] is that new moon which, for the sake of method, is supposed to have preceded the beginning of the world by one year. This new moon, or noumenia [νουμηνια], fell on October 7 in the year of the Julian period 953. From this epoch the Jewish calculation always proceeds.

units.la: XIV. 4. Calculus hic per cyclos Decemnovales à Molad Tohu collectos perficitur.
units.tr: XIV. 4. This calculation is carried out by nineteen-year cycles counted from Molad Tohu.

units.la: 1. Cyclus Decemnovalis five enneadecaeteris Judaica 19 annis constat, è quibus 12 sunt communes, 7 Embolimæi: Dies colligit 6939, hor. 6. 595. five hor. 16. 33′. 3″. 20‴. cyclus autem Julianus dies colligit 6939. hor. 18. Differentia cycli Juliani & Judaici hor. 1. 26′. 56″. 40‴. five Judaicè hor. 1. 485. Tanto temporis intervallo cyclus Julianus Judaicum superat. Quocirca pro singulis cyclis Judaicis completis hor. 1. 485 detrahenda sunt, ut verus neomeniæ locus in anno Juliano juxta Judaicos eruatur epilogifmos.
units.tr: 1. The Jewish nineteen-year cycle (enneadecaeteris) consists of 19 years, of which 12 are common and 7 embolismic. It gathers 6939 days, 6 hours, 595 helakim, or 16 hours, 33′ 3″ 20‴. The Julian cycle, however, gathers 6939 days and 18 hours. The difference between the Julian and Jewish cycles is 1 hour, 26′ 56″ 40‴, or in Jewish reckoning 1 hour and 485 helakim. By this interval of time the Julian cycle exceeds the Jewish. Accordingly, for each completed Jewish cycle, 1 hour and 485 helakim must be subtracted, so that the true place of the new moon in the Julian year may be found by Jewish calculation.

units.la: XV. 5. In cyclo Judaico hi anni sunt Embolimæi 3. 6. 8. 11. 14. 17. 19.
units.tr: XV. 5. In the Jewish cycle these years are embolismic: 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 17, 19.

units.la: XVI. 6. In hoc calculo characteres potissimùm observantur, qui sic fe habent.
units.tr: XVI. 6. In this calculation the characters chiefly observed are these, which stand as follows.

units.la: Character f. hor. hel.
units.tr: Character: weekday, hour, helakim.

units.la: 1. Mensis est •I. 12. 793.
2. Anni communis 4. 8. 876.
units.tr: 2. Common year: 4. 8. 876.

units.la: 3. Embolimæi 5. 21. 589.
units.tr: 3. Embolismic year: 5. 21. 589.

units.la: 4. Cycli decemnov. 2. 16. 595.
units.tr: 4. Nineteen-year cycle: 2. 16. 595.

units.la: 5. Molad tohu 2. 5. 204.
units.tr: 5. Molad Tohu: 2. 5. 204.

units.la: 6. Excesus Juliani, d. h. hel.
units.tr: 6. Excess of the Julian [year], in days, hours, helakim:

units.la: 1. In anno communi 10. 21. 204.
units.tr: 1. In a common year: 10. 21. 204.

units.la: 2. In cyclo decemnov. 0. 1. 485. d. h. hel.
units.tr: 2. In the nineteen-year cycle: 0. 1. 485.

units.la: 7. Excessus Judaici in anno Embolimæo 18. 15. 589.
units.tr: 7. Excess of the Jewish [year] in an embolismic year: 18. 15. 589.

units.la: 1. Universus Judæorum computus per hosce characteres administratur, qui numeros septenarios abjiciendo plerunque colliguntur. Ex. gr. mensis est dierum 29. hor. 12. 793, abjice quatuor hebdomades sive 28, & relinquetur character mensis d. 1. 12. 793 hinc pro charactere mensis in tabulas suas rationales referunt 1. 12. 793. Annus communis est dier. 354. hor. 8. 876. abjectis 50 septimanis, anni communis character fit, 4. 8. 876. Et eâdem ratione characteres anni Embolimæi & cycli decemnovalis exuuntur. Character Molad tohu constituitur 2. 5. 204, eò quòd novilunium istud prolepticum accidit feriâ 2, horâ 5. 204 à sextâ horâ post meridiem Hierosolymis. Character excessus Juliani in cyclo est 0. 1. 485 quia tantus est excessus cycli Juliani supra Judaicum. Et ob eandem rationem character excessûs Juliani in anno communi est 10. 21. 204. Character denique excessûs Judaici in anno Embolimæo est 18. 15. 589. eò quòd annus Judaicus Embolimæus Julianum excedat diebus 18 horis 15. 589. nam annus Julianus est dier. 365. hor. 6. Judaicus Embolimæus dier 383. hor. 21. 589. differentia d. 18 15. 589.
units.tr: 1. The whole Jewish computation is carried out by these characters, which are usually obtained by casting out the sevens. For example, the month has 29 days, 12 hours, 793 helakim; cast out four weeks, that is 28 days, and the character of the month remains: 1 day, 12 hours, 793 helakim. Hence they enter 1. 12. 793 in their working tables as the character of the month. The common year has 354 days, 8 hours, 876 helakim; with 50 weeks cast out, the character of the common year becomes 4. 8. 876. By the same method the characters of the embolismic year and of the nineteen-year cycle are worked out. The character of Molad Tohu is 2. 5. 204, because that new moon, reckoned backwards, fell on feria 2 at 5 hours and 204 helakim after the sixth hour of the afternoon at Jerusalem. The character of the excess of the Julian [year] in the cycle is 0. 1. 485, because this is the amount by which the Julian cycle exceeds the Jewish. For the same reason the character of the excess of the Julian [year] in a common year is 10. 21. 204. Finally, the character of the excess of the Jewish [year] in an embolismic year is 18. 15. 589, because the Jewish embolismic year exceeds the Julian by 18 days, 15 hours, 589 helakim. For the Julian year is 365 days, 6 hours, while the Jewish embolismic year is 383 days, 21 hours, 589 helakim; the difference is 18 days, 15 hours, 589 helakim.

units.la: XVII. Ex hisce præcognitis calculus Judaicus ita administratur. Annum propositum dividas per 19, & primò cyclos completos in quotiente datos multiplices in characterem cycli 2. 16. 595. deinde annos completos in residuo datos multiplices, communes quidem in 4. 8. 876. Embolimæos in 5. 21. 589. harum multiplicationum productis adjicias characterem Molad tohu summa, abjectis omnibus septenariis è diebus, est Character neo-meniæ Tisri quæsitæ.
units.tr: XVII. From these preliminary facts the Jewish calculation is carried out as follows. Divide the year in question by 19, and first multiply the complete cycles given in the quotient by the character of the cycle, 2. 16. 595; then multiply the complete years given in the remainder, common years by 4. 8. 876 and embolismic years by 5. 21. 589. To the products of these multiplications add the character of Molad Tohu; the sum, with all the sevens cast out of the days, is the character of the sought new moon of Tishri.

units.la: 1. Ex. gr. Proponatur annus Judaicus 5428 qui hoc anno Christi 1667 init, ut ejus initium sive neomeniam Tisri calculemus. Calculus ita procedit. char.cycli. | anni com. | an. embol. 19)5428(285. | 2. 16. 595. | 4. 8. 876. | 5. 21. 589. 38 | 285. | 8. | 4. 162 | 3. 13. 15. | 6. 22. 528. | 2. 14. 196. 152 108. | £. h. hel. 95. | Character 285 cyclorum | 3. 13. 15. 13. | 8 annorum communium | 6. 22. 528. 4 Embolimæorum | 2. 14. 196. Molad tohu addendus | 2. 5. 204. Summa | 1. 6. 943.
units.tr: 1. For example, let the Jewish year 5428, which begins in the Christian year 1667, be proposed, so that we may calculate its beginning, or new moon of Tishri. The calculation proceeds thus: 19)5428(285; character of the cycle 2. 16. 595; common years 4. 8. 876; embolismic years 5. 21. 589. Working: 38, 152, 108, 95 remainder 13. Character of the 285 cycles: 3. 13. 15. Character of 8 common years: 6. 22. 528. Character of 4 embolismic years: 2. 14. 196. Molad Tohu to be added: 2. 5. 204. Sum: 1. 6. 943.

units.la: 1. In hoc, uti vides, exemplo primo annum propositum 5428 divido per 19. Quotus est 285, ergò à Molad tohu ad hunc annum elapsi sunt cycli 285 completi, Residuum divisionis est 13. Ergò annus propositus est decimus tertius cycli currentis, adeò ut de cyclo 286 12 anni completi sunt. Deinde cyclos completos 285 multiplico in characterem cycli 2. 16. 595. Productum abjectis omnibus septimanis est 3. 13. 15. Ergò character 285 cyclorum, est feria 3. horæhel. 15. Idem etiam in annis expansis repeto, qui in residuo divisionis exhibentur. Residuum istud est 13. Hic igitur annus est 13 cycli currentis. Verùm annus currens non sumendus est sed completi. Anni completi sunt 12, è quibus ut è prædictis constat, quatuor sunt Embolimæi, putà 3. 6 8. 11. reliqui octo communes. Octo hosce communes annos multiplico in characterem anni communis 4. 8. 876. & productum abjectis hebdomadi-bus bus est 6. 22. 528. i. e. d. 6. hor. 22. hel. 528. Et tandem ad annos Embolimæos me confero qui cum quatuor sunt, quater multiplico characterem anni Embolimæi 5. 21. 589. & productum est 2. 14. 196. Harum denique trium multiplicationum productis cyclorum, annorum communium, & Embolimæorum characteres continentibus, collectis aggrego characterem Molad tohu 2. 5. 204. Summa omnium horum characterum abiectis omnibus septimanis è diebus est 1. 6. 943. Ergo annus hic Judaicus 5428 incipit feriâ, i. e. horâ 6. helak. 943 post sextam horam pomeridianam Hierosolymis.
units.tr: 1. In this first example, as you see, I divide the year proposed, 5428, by 19. The quotient is 285, so 285 complete cycles have elapsed from Molad Tohu to this year, and the remainder of the division is 13. Therefore the year proposed is the thirteenth year of the current cycle, so that 12 years of the current cycle are complete. Next I multiply the 285 complete cycles by the character of the cycle, 2. 16. 595. With all the weeks cast out, the product is 3. 13. 15. Therefore the character of the 285 cycles is feria 3, hour 13, helakim 15. I repeat the same procedure for the years set out in the remainder of the division. That remainder is 13, so this year is the 13th of the current cycle. But the current year is not to be taken, only the complete years. There are 12 complete years, of which, as is clear from what was said above, four are embolismic, namely years 3, 6, 8 and 11; the remaining eight are common. I multiply these eight common years by the character of a common year, 4. 8. 876, and with the weeks cast out the product is 6. 22. 528, that is, 6 days, 22 hours, 528 helakim. Finally I turn to the embolismic years, which are four in number; I multiply the character of an embolismic year, 5. 21. 589, four times, and the product is 2. 14. 196. Lastly, I add together the products of these three multiplications, which contain the characters of the cycles, of the common years and of the embolismic years, and add the character of Molad Tohu, 2. 5. 204. The sum of all these characters, with all the weeks cast out of the days, is 1. 6. 943. So this Jewish year 5428 begins on feria 1, that is, at hour 6 and 943 helakim after the sixth hour of the afternoon at Jerusalem.

units.la: 2. Aliud exemplum, proponatur annus Judaicus 3831. ut neomeniæ Tisri characterem Arithmeticè calculemus, qui quidem erat Æræ Christianæ septuagesimus. Calculus sic administratur. 19)3831.(201 char.cycli. anni com. embol. 38 2. 16. 595. 4. 8. 876. 5. 21. 589. cq31 201. 7. 4. 19. 1. 14. 795. 2. 13. 732. 2. 14. 196. 12 Character cyclorum 201 — 1. 14. 795. Annorum comm. 7 — 2. 13. 732. Embolimæorum 4 — 2. 14. 196. Molad tohu add. — 2. 5. 204. Summa. 1. 23. 847.
units.tr: 2. Another example: let the Jewish year 3831 be proposed, so that we may calculate arithmetically the character of the new moon of Tishri, which fell in the seventieth year of the Christian era. The calculation is set out thus: 19)3831(201; character of the cycle 2. 16. 595; common years 4. 8. 876; embolismic years 5. 21. 589. Working: 38, 43, 51, 31, remainder 7. Character of the 201 cycles: 1. 14. 795. Of 7 common years: 2. 13. 732. Of 4 embolismic years: 2. 14. 196. Molad Tohu to be added: 2. 5. 204. Sum: 1. 23. 847.

units.la: Character neomeniæ Tisri hoc anno erat 1. 23. 847. hoc est Annus propositus 3831 cœpit feriâ 1. hor. 23. hel. 847. ab epochâ Judaicâ.
units.tr: The character of the new moon of Tishri in this year was 1. 23. 847. That is, the proposed year 3831 began on feria 1, at hour 23 and 847 helakim, reckoning from the Jewish epoch.

units.la: 3. Si annus propositus per 19 divisus ultra cyclos completos relinquat tantum unitatem, cycli tantum in Characterem cycli multiplicandi sunt, & producto characterem Molad tohu adjiciendus. Sic annus Judaicus 4086 per 19 divisus in quoto dat 215, in residuo, L. ♃. Quandoquidem igitur anni completi tantum assumendi sunt, non currens, cyclos istos 215 multiplico in characterem cycli 2: 16. 595 & producto 4.6.485. addo characterē Molad tohu 2.5.204. summa 6.11. 689 est character neomeniae Tisri istius anni.
units.tr: 3. If the year proposed, when divided by 19, leaves only a unity beyond the complete cycles, then only the cycles are to be multiplied by the character of the cycle, and the character of Molad Tohu added to the product. Thus the Jewish year 4086, divided by 19, gives 215 in the quotient and 1 in the remainder. Since therefore only complete years are taken, not the current one, I multiply these 215 cycles by the character of the cycle, 2. 16. 595, and the product is 4. 6. 485. I add the character of Molad Tohu, 2. 5. 204; the sum, 6. 11. 689, is the character of the new moon of Tishri of that year.

units.la: 4. Ob eandem etiam rationem si nihil in residuo relinquatur, sed annus propositus sit ultimus cycli currentis, cycli in quoto dati, unitate mutilandi sunt, & tunc in characterem cycli multiplicandi, & anni praeterea 18 completi in characteres annorum communium & Embolimaeorum, non secus ac si quotus unitate minor fuisset, & residuum 19.
units.tr: 4. For the same reason, if nothing is left in the remainder, but the year proposed is the last year of the current cycle, the cycles given in the quotient are to be reduced by one unit, and then multiplied by the character of the cycle; and in addition, the 18 complete years are reckoned as common and embolismic years, just as if the quotient had been one less and the remainder 19.

units.la: XVIII. Ut diem in anno Juliano assequaris in quem neomenia Tisri convenit, cyclos elapsos multiplices in o. 1. 485, & annos completos communes quidem in d. 10. 31. 204 Embolimaeos in d. 18, 15. 589 hujus ultimae multiplicationis productum è producto secundae detrahes, & residuum ad productum primae multiplicationis addes, summam diernm ex Octob. 7. aufer, & relinquetur dies Julianus in quem neomenia Tisri quaesita incidit.
units.tr: XVIII. To find the day in the Julian year on which the new moon of Tisri falls, multiply the completed cycles by d. 0. h. 1. 485, and the completed common years by d. 10. h. 31. 204, and the completed embolismic years by d. 18. h. 15. 589. Subtract the product of this last multiplication from the product of the second, add the residue to the product of the first, subtract the sum of the days from October 7, and the Julian day on which the sought new moon of Tisri falls will remain.

units.la: 1. Cycli completi in d. o. h. 1. 485. ducendi sunt, propterea quòd tantò cyclus Judaicus à Juliano excedit. Anni communes in dies 10. h. 31. 204, eò quod tantus est excessus anni Juliani in Judaicum communem; at Embolimaei in dies 18. h. 15. 589 idcirco multiplicandi sunt, quòd annus Judaicus Embolimaeus tantò Julianum excedat; hujus autem ultimae multiplicationis productum è prioris producto subducendum est, eò quod quantò major sit excessus anni Judaici Embolimaei supra Julianum, tantò minor fit excessus anni Juliani supra Judaicum. Hoc autem residuum ad primae multiplicationis productum aggregandum est, quoniam summa totum dabit excessum anni Juliani supra Judaicum, tam in cyclis, quàm annis completis, quae fi subtrahatur ex Octob. 7 diem relinquet Julianum quo neomenia quæsita contigit, eò quòd epocha à qua calculus hic Judaicus supputatur, in Octob. 7 fixa fuit, anno mundi conditum juxta computum Judaicum antecedente.
units.tr: 1. The completed cycles must be multiplied by d. 0. h. 1. 485, because the Jewish cycle exceeds the Julian by that amount. The common years are multiplied by d. 10. h. 31. 204, because that is the excess of the common Jewish year over the Julian. The embolismic years are multiplied by d. 18. h. 15. 589, because the embolismic Jewish year exceeds the Julian by that amount. The product of this last multiplication must be subtracted from the product of the first, because the greater the excess of the embolismic Jewish year over the Julian, the smaller the excess of the Julian year over the Jewish. This residue must be added to the product of the first multiplication, since the sum will give the whole excess of the Julian year over the Jewish, both in cycles and in completed years. If this is subtracted from October 7, it leaves the Julian day on which the sought new moon fell, because the epoch from which this Jewish calculation is reckoned was fixed on October 7, in the year preceding the creation of the world according to the Jewish reckoning.

units.la: 2. Ex gr. In exemplo primo proposito, anno Judaico 5428, cycli completi erant 285, anni 12. Itaque primo 285 multiplico in d. o. 1. 485, productum est d. 17. 4. 1065. ex annis 12 completis octo sunt communes, & quatuor Embolimæi: Igitur octo communes annos duco in d. 10. 21. 204. productum est d. 87. 1. 552. deinde 4 Embolimæos multiplico in d. 18. 15. 589. & productum d. 74. 14. 196. subduco è priori producto 87. 1 552. residuum est dies 12. 11. 3 56. quod cum primæ multiplicationis producto d. 17. 4. 1065 collectum, dat dies 29. 16. 341. hoscę dies 29 subduco ex Octob. 7. sive additis etiam Septembris diebus ex 27. & relinquitur dies Septembris 8. Igitur annus hic Judaicus 5428 init hoc anno Christi 1667, ἐσχάτῳ Sept. 8. Idque feriâ 1. h. 6. 943 ab epochâ diei Judaicâ, ut è præcedenti regulâ constat.
units.tr: 2. For example, in the first example proposed, in the Jewish year 5428, there were 285 completed cycles and 12 years. First I multiply 285 by d. 0. h. 1. 485, which gives d. 17. h. 4. 1065. Of the 12 completed years, eight are common and four embolismic. So I multiply the eight common years by d. 10. h. 21. 204, which gives d. 87. h. 1. 552. Then I multiply the four embolismic years by d. 18. h. 15. 589, which gives d. 74. h. 14. 196. I subtract this from the earlier product, 87. 1. 552, and the residue is d. 12. h. 11. 356. Added to the product of the first multiplication, d. 17. h. 4. 1065, this gives d. 29. h. 16. 341. I subtract these 29 days from October 7, or, adding the days of September as well, from 27 (of September), and there remains September 8. So this Jewish year 5428 began in the year of Christ 1667, at the end [ἐσχάτῳ] of September 8, and that on the second feria, with h. 6. 943 from the Jewish epoch of the day, as follows from the preceding rule.

units.la: 3. Sic in altero exemplo sive anno Judaico 3831. cycli completi erant 201, anni 11. cycli 201 in o. 1. 485. multiplicati producunt dies 12. 3. 285. Anni communes 7 in d. 10. 21. 204 ducti producunt dies 76. 4. 348. & Embolimæi 4 in 18. 15. 589 multiplicati producunt 74. 14. 196. quibus è producto secundæ multiplicationis detractis residuum fit d. 1. 14. 152 cui productum primæ multiplicationis sive 12. 3. 285 cùm addideris, fient dies 13. 17. 437. Aufer dies hoscę 13 ex Octob. 7. & reliquus fit dies Sept. 24. Annus itaque Judaicus 3831 iniit anno Christi 70, Sept. 24. & quidem feriâ 1. 23. 847. ut è prædictis liquet. At quoniam in hoc exemplo pluisquam horæ 18 colligitur, minuntur horæ 23. 847 hinc, ut antè à monuimus, feria secunda sumenda est, ac si horæ istæ 23 solidum diem complevirint. Iniit igitur annus hic Judaicus juxta Astronomicum Judæorum calculum Sept. 24. feriâ 2. cyclus solis erat 23. Lit. Dom. G. character Sept. 24. A. Erat ergò Feria secunda. Quòd si dies sic inventus in feriam antè calculatum non rectè incideritt, per feriam istam corrigendus est. Ut si hoc anno calculus ad Sept. 25. nos direxisset, dies tamen 24 assumenda fuisset, propterea quòd ista, non 25 est Feria secunda.
units.tr: 3. Likewise in the other example, the Jewish year 3831: there were 201 completed cycles and 11 years. The 201 cycles multiplied by d. 0. h. 1. 485 give d. 12. h. 3. 285. The 7 common years multiplied by d. 10. h. 21. 204 give d. 76. h. 4. 348. The 4 embolismic years multiplied by d. 18. h. 15. 589 give d. 74. h. 14. 196. When I subtract these from the product of the second multiplication, the residue is d. 1. h. 14. 152. When I add this to the product of the first multiplication, namely 12. 3. 285, the result is d. 13. h. 17. 437. Subtract these 13 days from October 7, and the remainder is September 24. So the Jewish year 3831 began in the year of Christ 70, on September 24, and indeed on the first feria, with 23. 847 hours. As is clear from what has been said, since in this example more than 18 hours are collected, these 23 hours 847 parts are rounded up, as we noted before, so that the second feria must be taken, as if these 23 hours had completed a whole day. Therefore this Jewish year began, according to the Jewish astronomical calculation, on September 24, on the second feria. The cycle of the sun was 23. The Dominical letter G, the character for September 24 is A. It was therefore the second feria. But if the day found in this way does not fall correctly on the feria calculated before, it must be corrected by that feria. For example, if in this year the calculation had brought us to September 25, the day 24 would nevertheless have to be taken, because that day, not 25, is the second feria.

units.la: 4. Deprehensâ neomeniâ Tisri, reliquorum mensium neomeniæ facillimè dignoscantur. Nam ex. gr. hoc anno Christi 1667, annus Judaicus 5428 cœpit Sept. 8. Si scire vellem in quem diem Julianum incidit neomenia Marheshvan, mensium laterculum consulo, & invenio Tisri 30 habere dies. Igitur ad Sept. 8. addo 30. summa est 38. Ergo neomenia Marhesh van accidit die 38 à Kal. Sept. sive Oct. 8. Si characterem neomeniæ Marheshvan tenerem, ad characterem Tisri adjicio characterem unius mensis, eò quòd à neomeniâ Tisri ad neomeniam Marheshvan unicus mensis intercedit, character neomeniæ Tisri est 1. 6. 943. character mensis est 1. 12. 793. Aggregatum horum characterum est 2, 19.656. qui character est neomeniæ Marheshvan. Sed quoniam horæ sunt 19, hinc proxima feria sumenda est, Incidet ergo neomenia Marheshvan in Octob. 8. fer. 3. Litera Dom. est F. character Octob. 3. A. Est ergo Feria tertia.
units.tr: 4. Once the new moon of Tisri has been established, the new moons of the other months are very easily identified. For example, in this year of Christ 1667, the Jewish year 5428 began on September 8. If I want to know on what Julian day the new moon of Marheshvan falls, I consult the table of months and find that Tisri has 30 days. So I add 30 to September 8, and the sum is 38. Therefore the new moon of Marheshvan falls on the 38th day before the Kalends of September, that is, October 8. If I had the character of the new moon of Marheshvan, I would add the character of one month to the character of Tisri, since only one month lies between the new moon of Tisri and the new moon of Marheshvan. The character of the new moon of Tisri is 1. 6. 943; the character of a month is 1. 12. 793. The sum of these characters is 2. 19. 656, which is the character of the new moon of Marheshvan. But since there are 19 hours, the next feria must be taken, so the new moon of Marheshvan falls on October 8, on the third feria. The Dominical letter is F, the character of October 3 is A. It is therefore the third feria.

units.la: 5. In altero exemplo anni Judaici 3831 neomenia Tisri in Sept. 24. anno Christi 70 concurrit. Neomeniam Nisan haberem. Dies Sept. 24 est 267 à Kal. Jan. A neomenia Tisri ad neomeniam Nisan dies 277 effluunt, ut è mensium laterculo patet. Igitur ad 267 aggrego 177, è summâ 444 abjicio dies unius anni Juliani, sive 365, residuum est 79. Ergo neomenia Nisan incidit in diem 79 à Kal. Jan. i. e. Martii 20. anno Christi 71. Si characterem etiam hujus neomeniæ deprehenderem, quoniam Nisan hoc anno, ut communi, est septimus à Tisri inclusive, hinc sexies multiplico characterem mensis 1. 12. 793 productum, abjeƈto numero septenario, 2. 4. 438 est sex mensium character. Cui cum adjicerem characterem Tisri qui hoc anno per calculum fuit 1. 23. 847, aggregatum est 4. 4. 205. Ergo anno hoc Judaico neomenia Nisan Astronomicè Mart. 20. Feriâ 4. horâ 4. 205 accidet, anno Christi 71. cyclus solis fuit 24. Lit. Dom. F. character Martii 20 B. Erat ergo Feria quarta. Pascha celebratum est die 15 hujus mensis, i. e. April. 3. Feriâ. 4. Nam neomenia Nisan & Pascha semper eandem in feriam coincidunt.
units.tr: 5. In the other example, the Jewish year 3831, the new moon of Tisri coincided with September 24 of the year of Christ 70. I want the new moon of Nisan. September 24 is the 267th day from the Kalends of January. From the new moon of Tisri to the new moon of Nisan, 277 days run out, as is clear from the table of months. So I add 177 to 267, and from the sum 444 I take away 365, the days of one Julian year, and the residue is 79. Therefore the new moon of Nisan falls on the 79th day from the Kalends of January, that is, March 20, in the year of Christ 71. If I were also to establish the character of this new moon, then, since Nisan in this common year is the seventh month counting Tisri inclusive, I multiply the character of a month, 1. 12. 793, six times, and, casting out the number seven, I get 2. 4. 438, the character of six months. If I add to this the character of Tisri, which by calculation this year was 1. 23. 847, the sum is 4. 4. 205. Therefore in this Jewish year the new moon of Nisan falls astronomically on March 20, on the fourth feria, at hour 4. 205, in the year of Christ 71. The cycle of the sun was 24. The Dominical letter is F, the character of March 20 is B. It was therefore the fourth feria. The Passover was celebrated on the 15th day of this month, that is, April 3, on the fourth feria. For the new moon of Nisan and the Passover always coincide on the same feria.

units.la: 6. Si deprehensâ neomeniâ Tisri, Paschalem etiam celebritatem quæ præcesserit, invenires ab inventâ Tisri neomeniâ, regulâ perpetuâ demas dies 163. Et dies residui Pascha præcedens indicabunt, idque in eodem Juliano, sed in antecedenti anno Judaico. Ex. gr. Anno Christi 70, Judaico 3831 neomenia Tisri convenit in Sept. 24. Hic dies est à Kal. Jan. 267, aufer 163, restant 104. Ergo anno Christi 70, Judaico 3830. Pascha celebratum est die 104 à Kal. Januariis, is est April. 14.
units.tr: 6. If, once the new moon of Tisri has been established, you wish to find the Paschal festival which preceded it, subtract 163 days from the new moon of Tisri found, by the perpetual rule. The days of the residue will indicate the Passover that preceded, in the same Julian year but in the preceding Jewish year. For example, in the year of Christ 70, Jewish year 3831, the new moon of Tisri coincided with September 24. This day is the 267th from the Kalends of January. Subtract 163, and 104 remain. Therefore in the year of Christ 70, Jewish year 3830, the Passover was celebrated on the 104th day from the Kalends of January, which is April 14.

units.la: 7. In anno Embolimæo Nisan est octavus à Tisri inclusivè propter mensem Veadar intercalatum. Quapropter in anno Embolimæo à Tisri ad Nisan ineuntem dies completi sunt 207 addendi ad diem Julianum, cui neomenia Tisri congruit, ut neomeniam Nisan assequamur. Cujus etiam characterem ut obtineamus, character mensis 1. 12. 793. septies ducendus est, & productum ad characterem Tisri aggregandum.
units.tr: 7. In an embolismic year, Nisan is the eighth month counting Tisri inclusive, because of the intercalated month Veadar. Therefore in an embolismic year, from Tisri to the beginning of Nisan, 207 completed days must be added to the Julian day on which the new moon of Tisri falls, in order to reach the new moon of Nisan. To obtain its character as well, the character of a month, 1. 12. 793, must be multiplied seven times, and the product added to the character of Tisri.

units.la: CAP. XV. De civili Judæorum anno.
units.tr: CAP. XV. On the civil year of the Jews.

units.la: Hactenus de Astronomico Judæorum anno, sequitur civilis. II: Civilis sive politicus Judæorum annus est, quo in rebus politicis utuntur.
units.tr: So far concerning the astronomical year of the Jews; the civil year follows. II: The civil or political year of the Jews is the one they use in public affairs.

units.la: I. ANNUS Astronomicus præter dies solidos, horas insuper, & scrupula colligit, & idcirco neque ad usum populi accommodari, neque in Kalendario facile disponi potest. Et hinc est quod alium etiam annum instituerunt aliquantulùm ab Astronomico diversum, & negotiis publicis adaptatum, qui propterea completis tantùm constat diebus, sine horis & scrupulis appensis. Quorum tamen exactam, ut haberent rationem, annumque suum ad res etiam Ecclesiasticas accommodarent, diem nonnunquam anno subducunt, alias adjiciunt. Quæ diei exemptio semper fit in mense Caslev, adjectio in Marheshvan, ut Caslev à pleno fiat cavus, & Marheshvan à cavo plenus.
units.tr: I. The astronomical year, besides whole days, also gathers hours and scruples, and so it can neither be readily adapted to the use of the people nor easily arranged in a calendar. Hence they instituted another year, somewhat different from the astronomical one and adapted to public business, which therefore consists only of complete days, with no hours or scruples added. Yet in order to take exact account of those hours and scruples, and to fit their year also to ecclesiastical matters, they sometimes subtract a day from the year and at other times add one. The removal of a day always happens in the month Kislev, and the addition in Marheshvan, so that Kislev, from full, becomes hollow, and Marheshvan, from hollow, becomes full.

units.la: III. Annus Judæorum civilis est etiam vel communis vel Embolimæus.
units.tr: III. The civil year of the Jews is either common or embolismic.

units.la: IV. Uterque vel deficiens est, vel ordinarius, vel abundans.
units.tr: IV. Each of these is either deficient, or ordinary, or abundant.

units.la: V. Annus deficiens est, cui in mense Caslev dies aufertur, ut communis sit dier. 353, Embolimæus dicrum 383.
units.tr: V. A deficient year is one from which a day is taken in the month Kislev, so that the common year has 353 days and the embolismic 383.

units.la: VI. Ordinarius, est qui more Astronomico dies colligit si communis sit 354. si Embolimæus 384.
units.tr: VI. An ordinary year is one that gathers days according to the astronomical manner: if common, 354; if embolismic, 384.

units.la: VII. Abundans est, cui dies in mense Marheshvan adjicitur, ut communis sit dier. 355. Embolimæus dicr 385.
units.tr: VII. An abundant year is one to which a day is added in the month Marheshvan, so that the common year has 355 days and the embolismic 385.

units.la: VIII. In omnibus hisce annis character præcipuè considerandus est. IX. Character anni communis munis deficientis / ordinarii / Abundantis — 3 / est 4 / 5 — Embolimei — deficientis / ordinarii / Abundantis — 5 / 6 / 7
units.tr: VIII. In all these years the character is especially to be considered. IX. Character of the common year: deficient / ordinary / abundant: 3 / 4 / 5; of the embolismic year: deficient / ordinary / abundant: 5 / 6 / 7.

units.la: I. Hi annorum characteres omnes abjiciendo septimanas colliguntur. Nam annus communis deficiens est dier. 353. aufer omnes septimanas & relinquitur character 3. Embolimæus dier. 383. qui per 7 divisi reliquos faciunt dies 5. Ergo anni Embolimæi deficientis character est 5. & sic in reliquis.
units.tr: I. These characters of the years are all found by rejecting weeks. For the deficient common year has 353 days; remove all the weeks and the character 3 remains. The embolismic year has 383 days, which divided by 7 leave 5 days. Therefore the character of the deficient embolismic year is 5, and so on for the rest.

units.la: X. Harumanni distinctionum causa est Feriæ translatio, quâ Feria anni ineuntis per calculum inventa ad aliam transfertur.
units.tr: X. The cause of these distinctions is the translation of the feria, by which the feria of the beginning year, found by calculation, is transferred to another.

units.la: XI Feriæ translatio est vel simplex vel complexa.
units.tr: XI. The translation of the feria is either simple or compound.

units.la: XII. Translatio simplex est, quâ Feria ad proximam transfertur.
units.tr: XII. A simple translation is one by which the feria is transferred to the next.

units.la: XIII. Hujus translationis quatuor assignantur causæ; Jah, Adu, Gatrad, & Batu thakpat.
units.tr: XIII. Four causes of this translation are assigned: Jah, Adu, Gatrad, and Batu thakpat.

units.la: XIV. Primò, Propter Jah transfertur Feria in proximam, quoties in Astronomico characteris Tisri calculo horæ 18, aut plus ultra solidos dies colligatur.
units.tr: XIV. First, on account of Jah the feria is transferred to the next whenever the astronomical character of Tishri gathers 18 hours, or more, beyond the complete days.

units.la: I. Literæ Hebraicæ ה׳ Jah denotant 18, hinc est quod hæc translationis causa Jah vocetur. Nimirum si in charactere Tisri calculando ultra dies completos horas insuper 18 vel plus colligimus, neomenia Tisri non eâdem die feriâ ve quam calculus representat, sed proximâ celebratur. Ut si character neomeniæ Tisri per calculum sit 2. 19.432. neomenia Feriâ istâ 2 non peragitur, sed in proximam rejicitur. Hæc Astronomica translationis causa vocatur, cujus & antea mentionem fecimus.
units.tr: I. The Hebrew letters ה׳ [Jah] denote 18, and hence this cause of translation is called Jah. Namely, if in calculating the character of Tishri we gather 18 hours or more beyond the complete days, the new moon of Tishri is not celebrated on the same feria that the calculation indicates, but on the next. For example, if the character of the new moon of Tishri by calculation is 2.19.432, the new moon is not held on feria 2 but is put off to the next. This is called the astronomical cause of translation, of which we also made mention earlier.

units.la: XV. Secundò, Propter Adu transfertur Feria; quoties per calculum sit prima, quarta vel sexta.
units.tr: XV. Second, on account of Adu the feria is transferred whenever by calculation it is the first, fourth or sixth.

units.la: I. Hæc translationis causa Adu vocatur, eò quòd tres istæ literæ in lingua Hebraicâ nostris numeralibus 1. 4. 6. respondent. Enimvero à Feriâ primâ, quartâ, vel sextâ annum suum nunquam auspicantur Judæi, quæ idcirco מְסוּלוֹת Rejicula vocantur, ut à neomeniâ Tisri figendâ rejectæ, idque ne Pascha contrà majorum traditionem in Feriam 2. 4. vel 6 incideret. Quatuor itaque tantummodò Feriæ neomeniam Tisri figendo relinquuntur, 2. 3. 5. 7. quæ itaque קְבִיעוּת Kebiæ à figendo nuncupantur.
units.tr: I. This cause of translation is called Adu, because these three letters in the Hebrew language correspond to our numerals 1, 4 and 6. Indeed the Jews never begin their year on the first, fourth or sixth feria. These are therefore called מְסוּלוֹת [Mesulot], "the rejected ones," as rejected from fixing the new moon of Tishri; and this is so that the Passover would not, contrary to the tradition of the elders, fall on feria 2, 4 or 6. Thus only four ferias remain for fixing the new moon of Tishri: 2, 3, 5 and 7. These are therefore called קְבִיעוּת [Kebiot], from "fixing."

units.la: 2. Sit itaque neomeniæ Tisri character 1. 14. 346. Feria prima est Rejicula, transfertur igitur in secundam, & sic si Feria Astronomicè calculata sit, quarta transfertur in quintam, si sexta in septimam.
units.tr: 2. Let the character of the new moon of Tishri be 1.14.346. The feria 1 is a rejected one, so it is transferred to the second; and so, if the calculated feria was the fourth, it is transferred to the fifth, and if the sixth, to the seventh.

units.la: XVI. Tertiò; Propter Gatrad transfertur Feria, quoties in anno communi Astronomicus Tisri character sit 3. 5. 204. vel aliquid amplius.
units.tr: XVI. Third, on account of Gatrad the feria is transferred whenever, in a common year, the astronomical character of Tishri is 3.5.204 or somewhat more.

units.la: 1. Feria tertia neomeniæ Tisri figendæ satis est idonea, sed nihilominus si ultra Feriam 3, in anno communi (non in Embolimæo) horæ 9. 204 vel amplius ut 3 9. 406. vel 3. 9. 1079, &c. neomenia Tisri transfertur. Vocatur hæc causa Gatrad quoniam hæ literæ גַּטְרָד Hebraicè denotant 3. 9. 204.
units.tr: 1. The third feria is quite suitable for fixing the new moon of Tishri; nevertheless, if beyond feria 3, in a common year (not an embolismic one), there are 9 hours and 204 parts or more, as 3.9.406 or 3.9.1079, etc., the new moon of Tishri is transferred. This cause is called Gatrad, since these letters גַּטְרָד [Gatrad] denote 3.9.204 in Hebrew.

units.la: XVII. Quartò; Propter Batu thakpat transfertur Feria, quoties proximo post Embolismum anno character Tisri sit 2. 15, 589. aut eò amplius.
units.tr: XVII. Fourth: because of Batu thakpat the day is postponed, whenever in the year after an Embolism the character of Tishri is 2. 15. 589 or more.

units.la: 1. Vocatur hæc causa Batu thakpat, propterea quòd hæ literæ בַּטּוּ חַקְפָּט Hebraicè valent 2. 15. 589. Obtinet autem hæc causa proximo tantùm post Embolismum anno, quo si character Tisri ἀσφαλῶς sit 2. 15. 589. vel 2. 15. 590. vel 2. 15. 1079, vel quomodocunque intrà 2. 15. 588. & 3. o. c. Feria ista secunda in tertiam transfertur.
units.tr: 1. This cause is called Batu thakpat, because these letters בַּטּוּ חַקְפָּט in Hebrew have the value 2. 15. 589. This cause applies only in the year immediately after an Embolism. If in that year the character of Tishri is securely [ἀσφαλῶς] 2. 15. 589, or 2. 15. 590, or 2. 15. 1079, or in any way within 2. 15. 588, and 3. o. c., then this second day is transferred to the third.

units.la: XVIII. Translatio complexa, est quà propter duarum simpli- cium causarum concursum, Feria Astronomica bis trans- fertur, primò in sibi, & deinde in ei proximam.
units.tr: XVIII. Compound transfer is when, because two simple causes coincide, the astronomical day is transferred twice: first onto the day that is itself, and then onto the day next to it.

units.la: 1. Ex. gr. Sit character Tisri per calculum inventus 7. 19. 4cc. hic duplici, sive complexâ opus est translatione, nam primò quoniam plus colligitur quàm horæ 18, neomenia transfertur à septimâ ad primam Feriam propter Jah: At prima Feria neomeniam non patitur propter Adu, transfertur igitur in secundam. Adeò ut quamvis Feria Astronomica sit septima, politica tamen quæ Kebia dicitur, est secunda.
units.tr: 1. For example, let the character of Tishri found by calculation be 7. 19. 4cc. This requires a double, or compound, transfer. First, since more than 18 hours are reckoned, the new moon is moved from the seventh day to the first day because of Jah. But the first day does not admit the new moon because of Adu, so it is moved to the second day. Thus, although the astronomical day is the seventh, the political day, which is called the Kebia, is the second.

units.la: XIX. Hisce præcognitis, qualitas anni Judaici facillimè dignoscatur, viz. num deficiens sit, ordinarius vel abundans.
units.tr: XIX. With these things known beforehand, the quality of the Jewish year is most easily discerned, namely whether it is deficient, regular, or abundant.

units.la: XX. Nam si neomeniam tam anni propositi quàm sequentis calculas, & politicas eorum Ferias sive Kebias figas, translatione, si opus sit, adhibitâ, & deinde Kebiam anni propositi à Kebia sequentis detrahas, numerus residuus est character qualitatis anni propositi.
units.tr: XX. For if you calculate the new moon both of the year in question and of the following year, and fix their political days, or Kebiot, using a transfer where necessary, and then subtract the Kebia of the year in question from the Kebia of the following year, the remaining number is the character of the quality of the year in question.

units.la: 1. Ex. gr. Scire vellem qualis sit hic annus Judaicus 5428. quem feriâ 1. 6. 943. incipere jam ostendimus; quapropter methodo propositâ neomeniam Tisri sequentis sive anni Judaici 5429 inquiro, cujus characterem invenio fore 5. 15. 739. Eumque incepturum esse Aug. 28. pro quo tamen sumendus est Aug. 27. ut in Feriam quintam incidat. Igitur annus propositus 5428 init Feriâ 1. sequens Feriâ 5. idque politicè pariter ac Astronomicè. At Feria prima anni 5428. est Rejicula propter Adu, transfertur itaque in secundam, sive Sept. 9. adeò ut anni 5428 Kebia sit 2, anni 5429 Kebia sit 5. demas igitur 2. Kebiam anni propositi ex 5 Kebiâ sequentis, & restat 3, character anni deficientis. Ergo annus Judaicus 5428 est communis deficiens.
units.tr: 1. For example, I wish to know what kind of Jewish year 5428 is, which we have already shown begins on Feria 1, day 6, 943. By the method proposed, I seek the new moon of Tishri of the following year, that is the Jewish year 5429, whose character I find to be 5. 15. 739, and that it will begin on August 28. For this, however, August 27 must be taken, so that it falls on Feria 5. Therefore the year in question, 5428, begins on Feria 1, and the following year on Feria 5, both politically and astronomically. But the first day of the year 5428 is a Rejicula because of Adu, and so it is transferred to the second day, that is September 9. Thus the Kebia of the year 5428 is 2, and the Kebia of the year 5429 is 5. Take away the 2, the Kebia of the year in question, from the 5, the Kebia of the following year, and 3 remains, the character of a deficient year. Therefore the Jewish year 5428 is a common deficient year.

units.la: 2. Sic etiam si quæratur qualis sit annus Judaicus 5429. hoc anno neomeniæ Tisri character, ut modò diximus, est 5. 15. 739. at annus proximus sive 5430 inibit Feriâ 4. 13. 248. Feria 4 est Rejicula propter Adu, transfertur igitur neomenia in Feriam 5, ut 5 sit Kebia sive neomenia politica istius anni 5430. sed & 5 est Kebia anni propositi 5429. Aufer 5 ex 5,restat o. i. e. 7. nam quoties nihil relinquitur, 7 pro Kebiâ sumenda est ; porro 7 est character anni Embolimæi abundantis. Ergo annus Judaicus 5429 est Embolimæus abundans.
units.tr: 2. Likewise, if one asks what kind of Jewish year 5429 is: in this year the character of the new moon of Tishri, as we have just said, is 5. 15. 739, but the next year, 5430, begins on Feria 4, 13. 248. Feria 4 is a Rejicula because of Adu, so the new moon is transferred to Feria 5, so that 5 is the Kebia, or political new moon, of that year 5430. But 5 is also the Kebia of the year in question, 5429. Subtract 5 from 5, and 0 remains, that is 7; for whenever nothing remains, 7 must be taken as the Kebia. Further, 7 is the character of an abundant Embolismic year. Therefore the Jewish year 5429 is an abundant Embolismic year.

units.la: CAP. XVI.
units.tr: CAP. XVI.

units.la: De Solari Judæorum anno.
units.tr: On the Solar Year of the Jews.

units.la: Actum est de Lunari Judæorum anno, sequitur Solaris.
units.tr: We have dealt with the lunar year of the Jews; the solar year follows.

units.la: II. Annus Judæorum Solaris ejusdem est quantitatis atque Julianus.
units.tr: II. The solar year of the Jews is of the same length as the Julian year.

units.la: III. Hic in 4 æquales partes distribuitur, Tekuphas vocatas, viz. in Tekuphăm Tisri, Tebeth, Nisan, & Tamuz.
units.tr: III. This is divided into four equal parts, called Tekuphas, namely the Tekupha of Tisri, of Tebeth, of Nisan, and of Tamuz.

units.la: I. VO X תקיפות Tekaphoth Hebraicè idem valet atque Græca Τροπαί, vid. puncta cardinalia, duo æquinoctia, totidémque solstitia. Hasce Tekuphas Judæi summâ superstitione observant, quæ itaque paucis explicandæ sunt; Totam autem earum doctrinam hisce regulis expediemus.
units.tr: I. Tekaphoth [תקיפות] in Hebrew means the same as the Greek tropai [Τροπαί], that is, the cardinal points: the two equinoxes and likewise the two solstices. The Jews observe these Tekuphas with the greatest superstition, so they must be explained briefly. We shall set out their whole doctrine by the following rules.

units.la: IV. 1. Tekupha Tisri æquinoctio Autumnali respondet, & committitur anno Juliano Bissextili Sept. 24. 9. primo post Bissextilem Sept. 24. 15. secundo Sept. 24. 21. tertio Sept 25. 3.
units.tr: IV. 1. The Tekupha of Tisri corresponds to the autumnal equinox and is fixed in a Julian Bissextile year at Sept. 24. 9. In the first year after a Bissextile at Sept. 24. 15. In the second at Sept. 24. 21. In the third at Sept. 25. 3.

units.la: V. 2. Tekupha Tebeth est solstitium brumale, & conficitur anno Juliano Bissextili Dec. 24. 16. 30. primo post Bissextilem Dec. 24. 22. 30'. secundo Dec. 25. 4. 30. tertio Dec. 25. 10. 30'.
units.tr: V. 2. The Tekupha of Tebeth is the winter solstice and is fixed in a Julian Bissextile year at Dec. 24. 16. 30. In the first year after a Bissextile at Dec. 24. 22. 30'. In the second at Dec. 25. 4. 30. In the third at Dec. 25. 10. 30'.

units.la: VI. 3. Tekupha Nisan æquinoctio verno respondens celebratur anno Bissextili Mart. 26. 0. 0. anno primo post Bissextilem Mart. 26. 6. secundo Mart. 26. 12. 0. tertio Mart. 25. 18. 0.
units.tr: VI. 3. The Tekupha of Nisan, corresponding to the vernal equinox, is observed in a Bissextile year at Mart. 26. 0. 0. In the first year after a Bissextile at Mart. 26. 6. In the second at Mart. 26. 12. 0. In the third at Mart. 25. 18. 0.

units.la: VII. 4. Tekupa Tamuz est solstitium æstivum, & peragitur anno Bissextili jun. 25. 7. 30'. primo post Bissextilem Jun. 25. 13. 30'. secundo Jun. 25. 19. 30'. tertio Jun. 25. 1. 30.
units.tr: VII. 4. The Tekupha of Tamuz is the summer solstice and is completed in a Bissextile year at Jun. 25. 7. 30'. In the first year after a Bissextile at Jun. 25. 13. 30'. In the second at Jun. 25. 19. 30'. In the third at Jun. 25. 1. 30.

units.la: 1. Hi sunt termini Tekuphis Judaicis præscripti, quos perraro, si unquam, transiliunt; in quibus præstituendis non dies tantùm sed & horæ horarumque scrupula observantur, quibus dies solidus post exactum quadriennium tacitè intercalatur. Quocirca si scire velles ipsum temporis articulum quo Tekupha quælibet propositta celebretur, inprimis observes num annus Julianus in quem convenit, sit Bissextilis, vel quotus post Bissextilem, & ex terminis hic definitis Tekuphàm tuam quàm citissimè invenies. Ex. gr. Scire vellem quonam tempore Judæi Tekuphàm Tisri celebrant hoc anno Christi 1667. hic est tertius post Bissextilem. Ergo juxta regulam primam committitur Tekupha Tisri Sept. 25. hor. 3. 21. Rosh hashana sive neomenia Tisri per præcedentem doctrinam figitur Sept. 9. Incidit ergo Tekupha Tisri in diem 17. hor. 3. ejusdem mensis ab epochâ diei Judaicâ, unde & Tekuphæ computantur.
units.tr: 1. These are the limits of the Tekuphas prescribed by the Jews, which they very rarely, if ever, pass beyond. In fixing them not only the days but also the hours and the scruples of hours are observed, by which a solid day is tacitly intercalated after every completed four-year cycle. Hence, if you wish to know the exact moment at which any proposed Tekupha is celebrated, you should first observe whether the Julian year to which it falls is a Bissextile year, or which year it is after a Bissextile. From the limits defined here you will find your Tekupha as quickly as possible. For example, suppose I want to know at what time the Jews celebrate the Tekupha of Tisri in this year of Christ 1667. This is the third year after a Bissextile. Therefore, according to the first rule, the Tekupha of Tisri is fixed at Sept. 25, hour 3, 21. The Rosh hashana, or new moon of Tisri, is fixed by the preceding doctrine at Sept. 9. Therefore the Tekupha of Tisri falls on the 17th day, hour 3, of the same month, reckoned from the Jewish epoch of the day, whence the Tekuphas are also computed.

units.la: CAP. XVII.
units.tr: CAP. XVII.

units.la: De Anno Arabico.
units.tr: On the Arabic Year.

units.la: Annus Arabicus est Lunaris vagus.
units.tr: The Arabic year is a wandering lunar year.

units.la: 1. ANNUS hic Arabicus vocatur & Muhammedicus, sive Muhammedamus, à Muhammede Arabum pseudoprophetâ, ut & annus sive anni Hegoce, quoniam ab epochâ Hegiræ, i.e. fugæ Muhammedis à Mecca ad Medinam supputantur. Hunc autem annum vagum sive solutum appello, propterea quòd nulla intercalationis fræno coercitus per omnes anni Solaris tempestates liberè divagatur.
units.tr: 1. This year is called Arabic and also Muhammedan, or Muhammedamus, from Muhammed, the Arab pseudo-prophet. It is also called the year of the Hegira, because its years are counted from the epoch of the Hegira, that is, the flight of Muhammed from Mecca to Medina. I call this year wandering, or unbound, because it is not restrained by any bridle of intercalation and roams freely through all the seasons of the solar year.

units.la: II. Esque vel Astronomicus vel civilis.
units.tr: II. The year is either astronomical or civil.

units.la: III. Annus Arabum Astronomicus est dier. 354. hor. 8. 48'.
units.tr: III. The astronomical Arabic year is 354 days, 8 hours, 48 minutes.

units.la: I. Ex Arabum sententiâ mensis quilibet Astronomicus est dier. 29. hor. 12. helak. 792. uno helek minor quam mensis Judaicus. Verùm dies 29. hor. 12. 792, sive dies 29. h. 12. 44'. duodecies multiplicata anni quantitatem producunt dier. 354. hor. 8. 48'.
units.tr: I. According to the Arabs, every astronomical month is 29 days, 12 hours, 792 helek, one helek less than a Jewish month. Indeed, 29 days, 12 hours, 792 helek (that is, 29 days, 12 hours, 44 minutes) multiplied twelve times gives the length of the year: 354 days, 8 hours, 48 minutes.

units.la: IV. Annus civilis est vel communis vel ϛαιτφμεσς.
units.tr: IV. The civil year is either common or embolimaean.

units.la: V. Annus communis est dierum 354, ϛαιτφμεσς 355.
units.tr: V. The common year has 354 days; the embolimaean year has 355.

units.la: VI. Dies iste intercalaris ad finem anni apponitur in annis πεμπαδεκαται 2. 5. 7. 10. 13. 15. 18. 21. 24. 26. 29.
units.tr: VI. That intercalary day is added at the end of the year in the years 2, 5, 7, 10, 13, 15, 18, 21, 24, 26, 29.

units.la: I. Quandoquidem annus Lunaris Astronomicus præter dies solidos 354 horas insuper 8. 48'. colligit, ut annus Arabum civilis Lunæ motibus consentiret, dies nonnunquam ex istis horis scrupulisque collectus addatur necesse est. Adjicitur autem iste dies perpetuò ad finem Dulheggiæ, qui ultimus est mensis, & idcirco ad anni finem.
units.tr: I. Since the astronomical lunar year gathers, beyond 354 whole days, a further 8 hours and 48 minutes, it is necessary, so that the civil Arabic year may agree with the motions of the moon, that a day be added from time to time out of these collected hours and minutes. This day is always added at the end of Dhu'l-Hijja, which is the last month, and so at the end of the year.

units.la: 2. Annos porro suos in triacontaeterides idcirco partiuntur, quòd anni Astronomici triginta completos tantùm dies colligunt, nullis relictis horis, horarúmve scrupulis. Enimverò si 354. 8. 48'. trigesies multiplicaveris, producentur dies 10631. 0. 0. Quælibet autem πεντακοσιαδεκαταμεις, undeviginti annos communes, & undecim ϛαιτφμεσς continet. Hi undecim Embolimæi anni sive ϛαιτφμεσι quibus dies ad finem aggregatur, in qualibet triacontaeteride sunt secundus, quintus, septimus, &c. uti superius describuntur.
units.tr: 2. They divide their years into cycles of thirty years for this reason: thirty astronomical years collect exactly whole days, with no hours or fractions of hours left over. Indeed, if you multiply 354 days, 8 hours, 48 minutes by thirty, you get 10631 days, 0 hours, 0 minutes. Each such cycle contains nineteen common years and eleven embolimaean years, that is, years with a day added to the end. These eleven embolimaean years, in each thirty-year cycle, are the second, fifth, seventh, and so on, as described above.

units.la: VII. Menses sunt 12 alternis 30 & 29 dierum, nisi quòd in anno Embolimeo Dulheggia pro 29 habet 30 dies.
units.tr: VII. The months are twelve, alternately of 30 and 29 days, except that in an embolimaean year Dhu'l-Hijja has 30 days instead of 29.

units.la: VIII. Mensium nomina, quantitas, ac ordo sic se habent.
units.tr: VIII. The names, lengths and order of the months are as follows.

units.la: 1. Menses hosce singulos auspicantur Arabes, non ab ipso novilunio, sed à primâ post coitum apparitione vespertinâ, quæ uno plerunque die serior est ipso novilunio, nonnunquam biduo. Et hinc est quod dies Arabum à solis occasu computantur, eò quòd dies mensis accipiuntur ab ortu Lunæ, & ortus Lunæ fit tempore occasûs solis, ut inquit Alfraganus in Rud. Astron. c. 1. Quam etiam ob rem hoc omnibus est commune, qui mensibus utuntur Lunaribus, ut Judæis & Atheniensibus non minùs quam Muhammedanis, ut à noĉte dies suos auspicentur.
units.tr: 1. The Arabs begin each of these months not from the new moon itself, but from the first evening appearance of the moon after conjunction. This is usually one day later than the new moon itself, and sometimes two. For this reason the Arabs count their days from sunset, because the days of the month are taken from the rising of the moon, and the rising of the moon takes place at the time of sunset, as Alfraganus says in his Rudiments of Astronomy, ch. 1. For this reason it is common to all who use lunar months, such as the Jews and the Athenians no less than the Muhammedans, to begin their days at night.

units.la: 2. Dies mensium post decimum quintum sæpe, semper post vigesimum ordine retrogrado numerantur, à Muhammedanis æque ac ab Atheniensibus. Ut hi enim post ἑνδεκα dicunt Δευτέρα, ἐννέα, &c. sic & Arabes primum mensis diem vocant Mustahal cui succeddit secundus Madeina, i. e. præteritorum, tertius Madeina, quartus Madeina, & sic deinceps usque ad vigesimum, post quem dicunt Decimum Bakeina eorum qui supersunt, sive relictorum, nonum Bakeina, octavum Bakeina, & sic retrorsum agunt usque ad finem mensis. Quinetiam vigesimus primus dies ab Eutychio dicitur, primus è decem ultimis diebus mensis, Eutych. tom. 2. p. 342. Nonnunquam post diem 15. quem Nassph, i. e. medium appellat Elmacinus hist. Sar. c. 1. retrorsùm procedunt, unde idem Elmacinus diem 18 Jomadæ prioris vocat 13 bakeina Jomadæ prioris, ibid. c. 12.
units.tr: 2. The days of the months after the fifteenth are often, and after the twentieth always, counted in reverse order, by the Muhammedans just as by the Athenians. For the Athenians, after eleven [ἑνδεκα], say second [Δευτέρα], nine [ἐννέα], and so on. So the Arabs also call the first day of the month Mustahal, followed by the second, Madeina, that is, of the past days; the third is Madeina, the fourth Madeina, and so on up to the twentieth. After that they say the tenth is Bakeina, of those that remain, or of the leftover days, the ninth Bakeina, the eighth Bakeina, and so they count backwards to the end of the month. Moreover, Eutychius calls the twenty-first day the first of the last ten days of the month, Eutychius, vol. 2, p. 342. Sometimes after the fifteenth day, which Elmacinus, History of the Saracens, ch. 1, calls the middle [Nassph], they proceed backwards; hence Elmacinus calls the eighteenth day of Jumada I the thirteenth Bakeina of Jumada I, ibid. ch. 12.

units.la: 3. Porrò tempora sua non per dies sed noctes supputant. Non enim dicunt primâ vel secundâ die sed nocte mensis cujuslibet, nec tot diebus sed noctibus quippiam actum suisse, ut inter legendos scriptores Arabicos sæpius animadverti.
units.tr: 3. Moreover, they reckon their times not by days but by nights. They do not say that something happened on the first or second day of any month, but on the night of it, nor that something was done in so many days but in so many nights, as I have often noticed in reading Arabic writers.

units.la: IX. Calculus anni Muhammedici dupliciter consideretur, vel enim proposito anno Muhammedico annus diésque Æræ Christianæ quæritur quo cœpit, vel è contrà proposito quotûs Æræ Christianæ anno, quæritur, quotus annus Muhammedicus in eum conveniat.
units.tr: IX. The calculation of a Muhammedan year may be done in two ways: either, given a Muhammedan year, we seek the year and day of the Christian era on which it began; or, conversely, given a year of the Christian era, we seek which Muhammedan year corresponds to it.

units.la: X. Ad primum perficiendum calculum primò dies, deinde feria, quâ anni mensesque singuli Muhammedani incipiunt, computanda est.
units.tr: X. To carry out the first calculation, one must first compute the day, and then the weekday on which each Muhammedan year and month begins.

units.la: XI. Quod ad diem inveniendam spectat hac utaris methodo. Annos Muhammedanos completos dividas per 30 & primò quotum multiplices in 7836, & deinde residuum etiam in eundem numerum ducas, & ejus productum divides per 30, cujus divisionis quotum addas ad productum primæ multiplicationis, summam dividas per 8766, & hujus divisionis quotum (unitate auctum si proximæ quotus excedat 196) subducas ex annis Muhammedanis completis primo divisis; residuum addas ad 622 & habebis annum Christi quo propositus init. Et denique ultimæ divisionis residuum per 24 dividas, quotum (unitate auctum si residuum sit majus quam 12) aufer è diebus 196, vel si major sit quàm 196 eum dimas ex 561, numerus relictus est dies à Kal. Jan. neomeniam Muharram precedens.
units.tr: XI. To find the day, use this method. Divide the completed Muhammadan years by 30, and multiply the first quotient by 7836. Then multiply the remainder by the same number and divide the product by 30. Add this second quotient to the product of the first multiplication, and divide the sum by 8766. Subtract the quotient of this division, increased by one unit if the next quotient exceeds 196, from the completed Muhammadan years first divided. Add the remainder to 622, and you will have the Christian year in which the proposed year begins. Finally, divide the remainder of the last division by 24. Subtract the quotient, increased by one unit if the remainder is greater than 12, from 196. If the remainder is greater than 196, subtract it from 561 instead. The number left is the number of days from January 1 to the new moon of Muharram, which precedes the proposed year.

units.la: 1. Hujus methodi rationem ut assequaris, primò tenendum est annos Julianos 30 dies colligere 1c957 h. 1a. totidem autem Arabicos (quorum 19 communes sunt, & 11.
units.tr: 1. To grasp the reason for this method, it must first be held that 30 Julian years collect 10957 days and 12 hours, and that as many Arabic years, of which 19 are common and 11 intercalary, make up 10631 days.

units.la: L Уmpiuusi) dies completos 1063 1. Aufer dies 1063 1 ex 1095 7 hor. 12. & restant dies 326. hor. 12. Quocirca anni Juliani 30, Arabicos totidem & dies præterea 326.h. 12. continent; adeò ut si hodie annus Julianus & Muhammedicus simul inirent, post annos 30, Arabicus annus citiùs iniret quàm Muhammedicus dieb. 326. h. 12. Dies 326 sh 24 ducti horas producunt 7824, quibus si addamus prædictas 12 horas quæ præter dies 326 annis 30 anticipantur, summa est 7836. Proposito igitur anno quovis Muhammedico cujus initium quæris, unitas ab eo auferenda est, ut anni completi habeantur, quos si per 30 dividas, quotus indigitabit quoties anni 30 à primo Hegiræ elapsi sunt, residuum annos completos triacontaeteridos currentis, si igitur hujus divisionis quotum ducas in 7836, numerus productus est horarum summa, quibus tot triacontaeterides Arabicæ ab anno Juliano retrovertuntur: At numerus divisionis residuus juxta regulam proportionis in 7836 ductus & deinde per 30 divisus, in quoto exhibebit horas etiam quibus anni currentis triacontaeteridos completi in anno Juliano retrorsùm aguntur, quas itaque si primæ multiplicationis producto aggregemus omnes horas in unam summam redactas teneamus, quibus anni Hegiræ completi (qui propositum præcedunt) ab annis Julianis concurrentibus superati, & idcircò retroacti sunt. Quapropter si istam horarum summam per 8766 (quot horæ in anno Juliano continentur) partiaris, quotus ostendet annos Arabicos à Julianis retroversos, quos si subducamus ex annis completis primò divisis sive propositum antecedentibus, & residuum addamus ad 622 (quoniam anno Christi 622 primus Hegiræ cœpit) annum Æræ Christianæ quàm proximè assequemur, quo annus propositum præcedens exiit, & quod idem est, quo propositus init. Et ut quotus hujus ultimæ divisionis annos completos indigitat retroactos, sic & numerus residuus horas insuper continet, quas si per 24 dividamus, in quoto dies colligentur auferendi (quibus tamen unitas addenda est quoties numerus post hanc divisionem residuus excedat 12) qui si pauciores sint quàm 195 ex 196 subducantur, hoc est à Julii 15 completo qui est dies 196 à Kal. Jan. numerus enim residuus est dies à Kal. Jan. quo ultimus ante propositum annus Muhammedicus exiit: proximo igitur propositus init. Sin dies isti plures sint quàm 196, mutuo sunt accipiendi dies unius anni Juliani, sive 365, qui cum 196 collecti efficiunt 561. Ex his igitur dies tuos 196 excedentes auser, & reliquus fit dies in anno praecedenti Juliano quo annus Muhammedicus tuum praecedens completur. Et hinc est quòd si dies per ultimam divisionem inventi excedant 196, alius insuper ab annis Christi subducendus est, vel quod idem valet, primae divisionis quotus unitate augendus, quoniam hi dies ut plures quàm 196 annos tuos Muhammedicos in alium annum retroagunt. Sed haec omnia exemplis clariora elucescent.
units.tr: Subtract 10631 days from 10957 days and 12 hours, and 326 days and 12 hours remain. Thus 30 Julian years contain 30 Arabic years and in addition 326 days and 12 hours. So if a Julian year and a Muhammadan year began together today, then after 30 years the Arabic year would begin sooner than the Julian by 326 days and 12 hours. Multiplying 326 days by 24 gives 7824 hours; if we add the 12 hours that exceed the 326 days, the sum is 7836. Therefore, for any Muhammadan year whose beginning you seek, subtract one unit so that completed years are obtained. Divide these by 30, and the quotient shows how many 30-year cycles have passed since the first year of the Hegira, while the remainder gives the completed years of the current 30-year cycle. Multiplying this quotient by 7836 gives the sum of hours by which that many Arabic cycles fall back from the Julian years. The remainder of the division, multiplied by 7836 according to the rule of proportion and then divided by 30, gives in the quotient the hours by which the completed years of the current cycle also fall back in the Julian year. If we add these to the product of the first multiplication, we have all the hours reduced to one sum, by which the completed Hegira years preceding the proposed year have been overtaken by the Julian years and so have been carried back. Therefore, if we divide this sum of hours by 8766, the number of hours in a Julian year, the quotient shows the Arabic years carried back against the Julian years. If we subtract these from the completed years first divided, that is, from those preceding the proposed year, and add the remainder to 622 (since the first year of the Hegira began in the Christian year 622), we shall come close to the Christian Era year in which the preceding year ended, which is the same as the year in which the proposed year begins. And as the quotient of this last division indicates the completed years carried back, so the remainder also contains hours. If we divide these by 24, the quotient gives the days to be subtracted (to which one unit must be added whenever the remainder after this division exceeds 12). If these days are fewer than 196, they are subtracted from 196, that is, from July 15 completed, which is day 196 counted from January 1, since the remainder is the day from January 1 on which the last Muhammadan year before the proposed one ended; the proposed year therefore begins the next day. But if these days are more than 196, one day of a Julian year, that is 365 days, must be borrowed, which together with 196 makes 561. Subtract from these the days exceeding your 196, and the remainder is a day in the preceding Julian year on which your preceding Muhammadan year ends. Hence, if the days found by the last division exceed 196, one more year must be subtracted from the years of Christ, or, what amounts to the same, the quotient of the first division must be increased by one unit, since these days carry your Muhammadan years back by more than 196 days into another year. But all these things will become clearer through examples.
